whatItIs.heading: What wildfire restoration means for Eaton Fire-affected homes
whatItIs.body: The Eaton Fire of January 2025 destroyed thousands of structures in Altadena and caused smoke, ash, and soot intrusion in a much larger number of homes that remained physically intact. Wildfire restoration in this context covers two distinct tracks. The first is structural restoration: debris removal, structural assessment, smoke remediation inside the shell, and full reconstruction from framing through finishes. The second—affecting the majority of surviving homes—is contamination remediation: professional cleaning of smoke-coated surfaces, HVAC system decontamination, content restoration or documentation for insurance, and air-quality verification with HEPA filtration equipment. Both tracks require IICRC-trained technicians, insurance-grade documentation, and equipment that consumer-grade cleaning cannot replicate. The compounds in wildfire smoke are chemically different from interior smoke and require specific treatment to reach clearance-level readings.

process.heading: How Gallagher supports Altadena homeowners after the Eaton Fire

steps.title: On-site assessment and safety check
steps.body: The crew arrives—within 60 minutes of dispatch—and evaluates the home across structural integrity, smoke and soot distribution, HVAC contamination, exterior ash load, and contents condition. The assessment produces a written scope that forms the basis of your insurance claim.

steps.title: Containment and exterior decontamination
steps.body: Ash and soot are removed from exterior surfaces—rooflines, gutters, decking, vents—before they migrate further indoors. HVAC systems are isolated. Containment barriers separate affected zones from unaffected interior spaces.

steps.title: Smoke, soot, and odor remediation
steps.body: IICRC-trained technicians clean interior surfaces using dry and wet methods appropriate to each material. Thermal foggers and hydroxyl generators neutralize odor compounds embedded in structural materials. HEPA air scrubbers run continuously until air-quality readings confirm clearance.

steps.title: Reconstruction and insurance claim documentation
steps.body: For structurally damaged homes, Gallagher manages the full rebuild—from framing and drywall through flooring, cabinetry, and paint. Insurance documentation is produced throughout the process: photo logs, written scope, moisture and air-quality readings, and line-item cost records for the adjuster.

signs.heading: Situations that require professional wildfire restoration in Altadena
signs.intro: If your home was in the Eaton Fire's impact zone, professional assessment is appropriate even if the structure looks intact.

items.title: Smoke odor that persists indoors days after the fire
items.body: Lingering smoke odor means compounds have penetrated porous materials—insulation, drywall, wood framing, upholstery. Opening windows redistributes the particles; it does not remove them.

items.title: Visible ash or soot on walls, ceilings, or floors
items.body: Fine wildfire ash carries heavy metals and chemical compounds from burned structures. Standard household cleaning disperses these particles into the air. HEPA-equipped removal is required.

items.title: HVAC ran during or after the fire event
items.body: Any system that operated while airborne ash was present has contaminated the entire ductwork and air handler. The system must be inspected, cleaned, and cleared before use.

items.title: Structural damage: char, burned roofing, compromised framing
items.body: Visible burn damage requires a structural assessment before any other restoration begins. Gallagher coordinates with engineers and municipal inspectors as needed before the rebuild phase starts.

items.title: Insurance adjuster has completed the estimate and you need a contractor
items.body: If the insurance company has already processed your claim but you still need a qualified restoration contractor to execute the scope, Gallagher works directly from adjuster documentation and can take over at any point in the process.

pricing.heading: Eaton Fire restoration pricing for Altadena homeowners
pricing.body: Costs depend on whether the home has structural fire damage or smoke and ash intrusion alone. Smoke remediation for a home that survived the Eaton Fire but needs professional decontamination—including HVAC cleaning and air-quality clearance—typically runs $1,500–$10,000 depending on square footage and contamination severity. Structurally damaged homes requiring partial or full reconstruction range from $15,000 into six figures for complete rebuilds. Gallagher Restoration Co. provides a free on-site assessment—no charge to show up, document, and give you a written scope. This assessment is what your insurance carrier needs for the claim file. Do not commit to a restoration contract before an independent written scope is in hand.

faqs.q: Does California homeowners insurance cover Eaton Fire smoke damage to homes that did not burn?
faqs.a: Standard California homeowners policies generally cover wildfire damage including smoke and soot intrusion, even in homes that did not burn directly. Coverage limits and deductibles vary. Gallagher Restoration Co. produces written scope documentation and coordinates directly with your adjuster to support the claim from day one.

faqs.q: Can I clean Eaton Fire ash and soot myself?
faqs.a: Wildfire ash contains heavy metals, chemical compounds from burned structural materials, and fine particulates at sizes that standard vacuum filters cannot capture. Household cleaning typically disperses these particles rather than removing them. HEPA-equipped equipment and appropriate chemical cleaning agents are required to reach safe clearance levels.

faqs.q: My home in Altadena was not in the direct burn zone. Do I still need professional help?
faqs.a: If your home was downwind of the Eaton Fire or you notice persistent smoke odor, visible ash, or indoor air symptoms, a professional assessment is warranted. Smoke intrusion, ash on exterior vents, and contaminated HVAC systems are common in homes well outside the direct burn perimeter.

faqs.a: Call (951) 541-0034 to schedule a free on-site assessment. Gallagher Restoration Co. documents the full scope—structural condition, smoke and soot distribution, HVAC status, contents—and produces a written report you can submit directly to your insurance carrier.
